reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents Forsage/xCore as an opportunity to earn money, with the speaker describing 50% or 100% returns and a caption claiming 500%. The earnings are tied to program positions and work by the viewer and an upliner, making it a promotional earnings claim connected to participation. The precise payout mechanism and whether any returns occurred remain unestablished.

citations.quote: Now we have a new opportunity launched named as xCore
now here your work your team work, your upliner upliner works xCore also provides income and takes all necessary positions 50%
every position will be paid 50 %

opening.argument: Judge, the earnings language deserves scrutiny, but it does not specify a guaranteed net return to a viewer. The speaker describes “50% distribution” and later says the program will give “50% or 100%”—alternative figures without stated payment conditions, costs, or a time period. [ASR_0001] Even the caption claiming 500% does not supply those missing terms. [F0064] There is no express risk warning here, but neither should an unexplained percentage be treated as proof that the speaker has offered a guaranteed investment outcome. On this record, the figures can be read as an imprecise description of how the program operates rather than a complete solicitation.

citations.quote: the program returns 50% distribution
this program will give you 50% or 100%

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies earnings claims, including the 500% caption. [F0064] But it also concedes that the payout mechanism and actual returns are unestablished. “Every position will be paid 50%” describes a claimed rule, not who funds a position or whether a viewer must pay to enter one. [ASR_0001] Team and upliner activity likewise does not, by itself, establish that commissions are financed by recruiting new participants. [ASR_0001] Those missing links matter before treating this short explanation as a demonstrated scam mechanism.

citations.quote: every position will be paid 50 %
now here your work your team work, your upliner upliner works xCore also provides income

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A missing payment schedule does not make the presentation neutral. The speaker introduces xCore as a “new opportunity,” then links the viewer’s earnings to an upliner’s work in the on-screen caption. [ASR_0001] [F0047] The 500% caption is an affirmative earnings pitch, not merely an undefined technical percentage. [F0064] The defense has identified uncertainties about the mechanism, but its quotations do not explain away the video’s promotion of income through participant relationships.

citations.quote: Now we have a new opportunity launched named as xCore

opening.argument: Judge, this is framed as an explanation of how a program works. The title begins “how to work forsage xQore program,” and the speaker says that in this short video he will tell viewers about the programs. [TITLE_0001] [ASR_0001] The captions identify a set of business programs and describe xQore as working on BNB Smart Chain. [F0024] [F0035] That instructional framing matters: describing positions and distribution is not the same as showing a viewer how to sign up, transfer funds, or recruit someone. The earnings language is promotional in tone, but the supplied excerpt leaves the steps for any such transaction unstated.

citations.quote: how to work forsage xQore program
In today's short video i will tell you about 5 program x3, x4, xxx, Xgole

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening treats the income statements as promotion, and they are plainly favorable. But a favorable account can still be an operational explanation. The speaker introduces a new program while describing how its distribution and positions supposedly work. [ASR_0001] [ASR_0001] Neither those statements nor the cited caption showing upliner-related earnings establishes an enrollment instruction or a requested payment. [F0047] The question is what this video shows, not what transactions might occur outside it.

citations.quote: Now we have a new opportunity launched named as xCore
every position will be paid 50 %

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling something an explanation does not negate its sales message. The title also says “How to Earn money,” while the speaker presents xCore as a “new opportunity.” [TITLE_0001] [ASR_0001] Most importantly, the caption tells viewers they will earn when they or their upliner work, and another claims the program earns them 500%. [F0047] [F0064] The defense’s tutorial excerpts do not turn those direct, participant-linked earnings claims into neutral technical instruction.

citations.quote: How to Earn money
Now we have a new opportunity launched named as xCore

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker identifies the subject as a network-marketing internet platform and discusses a business program operating on BNB Smart Chain. [ASR_0001] [F0035] Those descriptions do not certify the service as safe, but they also do not establish a fraudulent transfer. The excerpt says team and upliner work can provide income and that positions are paid; it does not say that a viewer must buy a position, that recruiting fees fund the payments, or that credentials should be handed over. [ASR_0001] [ASR_0001] A discussion of participant compensation may be ordinary business promotion. The crucial source of the money, rather than the mere existence of an upliner, remains unshown.

citations.quote: fastshare.io is one of the network marketing internet platform
now here your work your team work, your upliner upliner works xCore also provides income
every position will be paid 50 %

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening’s strongest point is the connection between upliner activity and earnings. [F0047] Yet it expressly leaves the payout mechanism unestablished. “Every position will be paid 50%” says nothing about whether payments come from sales, fees, or another source. [ASR_0001] The 500% caption is a striking claim, but it does not resolve that source-of-funds question either. [F0064] Suspicion about the business model is reasonable; treating the missing mechanism as established is not.

citations.quote: every position will be paid 50 %

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The video need not reveal its source of funds to show what it is promoting. Its title advertises earning money, the speaker calls xCore a new opportunity, and the caption promises earnings tied to the viewer’s and upliner’s work. [TITLE_0001] [ASR_0001] [F0047] The 500% caption reinforces that earnings pitch. [F0064] The defense is right that the precise payment mechanism is not established, but that gap does not turn these participant-linked earnings claims into an ordinary description of a product or service.
